label: <DEL> step of long sequences, gated by first token
explanation: Fires only on the delimiter step (t == L); it is never active in the original or copy phases (phase==1 gives recall 1.0 but precision 0.13). Within delimiter steps the rate rises steeply with sequence length: about 0 for L<=4, 0.1% at L=5, 6% at L=6, then 13-56% for L=7..9; L=9 holds 42% of the mass. Which delimiter steps fire depends on what the sequence contains, mostly the first original token (b, g, m, 0, h, 3, z, p are the most enriched; b alone covers 13% of mass). Secondary tokens such as m/0/z/1 in position 1 and x/v/m/digits elsewhere help a bit (more digits gives a slightly higher rate). Top activations are long sequences that start with b/m/z/p and contain x, m, v, 1 or 0. The token dependence looks like a graded, distributed code, so no simple token set separates it cleanly (dev F1 about 0.48, mass recall about 0.71).

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: b, m, g, 0, h, z; least: -, n, c, v) and the third original token (most: 1, x, m, c, v, q; least: k, g, r, 2); timing cues that raise it most: L=9 & t=9, phase=1, recall_idx=0.
